## Why

ADR-148 Decision 5 (SEED-11, A-13) splits `D-R10-MEMORY-1` under B3 option
C: the **events/enforcement leg** closes on enforcement evidence; the
**closeout-journal leg** stays shadow-only until its recorded trigger
(parallel ticket dispatch, a multi-worktree build, or a second host or
harness writing memory concurrently) fires. Until this row, a DEFERRALS
leading status token could be moved by nothing more than a dated prose
note — "last token wins" — with the event chain left to catch up by hand
(exactly what `7a2ff9fa` did to eight rows). This row makes the link
mechanical: a lead-token move without its appended transition event fails
the guard the CI `docs` job already runs.

## What this ships

- **`memory_guard.py` — the `transition-event` rule.** For every DEFERRALS
  row whose leading status token differs between BASE and HEAD, the same
  judged range must append an `obligation-event/1` chain to
  `docs/build/reports/obligations/events.jsonl` that runs the token from
  the old lead to the new — matching obligation id, matching
  `from_status`/`to_status`, each hop's `expected_previous_event` naming
  the head its predecessor left (the BASE head, or a migration anchor
  first appended in the range). One transition is the one-hop case; a
  contiguous multi-hop run witnesses a net flip through its recorded
  intermediate states. A migration anchor or journal blob is not a
  witness; wrong-obligation / wrong-status / wrong-predecessor near-misses
  are reported by id. Pre-ledger history is untouched: with no events
  ledger at BASE the rule is inapplicable and the legacy sanctioned shape
  stands. Violations report under `append-only`/`transition-event` and
  name the row id plus the exact fix.
- **`test_memory_guard.py`** — the fixture's `events.jsonl` gains a
  schema-valid `D-T1-1:e0` migration anchor so the rule has a BASE chain
  head to compare against; `_ev` learns `from_status`; nine cases pin the
  rule: unwitnessed flip, foreign-obligation event, wrong from/to, wrong
  predecessor (double-flagged by `chain`), anchor-not-a-transition,
  two-flips-one-witness, contiguous two-hop witness, broken-chain run, and
  pre-ledger history unjudged. The `7a2ff9fa` oracle test now asserts the
  rule fires on the historical defect it exists to prevent.
- **`replay_expected.csv`** — one reviewed `violation` row for `7a2ff9fa`
  (`append-only`/`transition-event` on `docs/tickets/DEFERRALS.md`) plus a
  `waived` sibling withdrawing the register's `transition-justified` clean
  cell — the derived row stays beside the adjudication (B4 review rule,
  never a silent re-baseline).
- **The split recorded.** `DEFERRALS.md`: `D-R10-MEMORY-1` lead →
  `DONE 2026-10-05` with the old cell preserved verbatim; successor row
  `D-R10-MEMORY-2` appended with `owner:`/`trigger:` and the
  `BL-091`/`D-R11-LATER-13` home. `events.jsonl`: `D-R10-MEMORY-2:e0`
  migration anchor (row sha recorded) + `D-R10-MEMORY-1:e1` transition
  (`OPEN → DONE`, `expected_previous_event: D-R10-MEMORY-1:e0`), citing
  ADR-148, P34.8's repair evidence and this row's rule.
- **SIG-MEM-003 re-verdicted** — `coverage-assessment/1`
  `SIG-MEM-003:r11-1` supersedes `:a1` with `MET-ENGINEERED(D-R10-MEMORY-2)`
  at the implementation domain; the matrix cell updates verdict, owed leg
  and routing (P32.8 → BL-091, the live home — P32.8 has landed).
- **Trigger evaluation** — recorded in `docs/build/runs/P34.30.md`:
  **not fired** (one dispatch lane `dispatchTarget: subagent`,
  single-worktree, one memory writer); the journal leg stays shadow.
- **Projection** regenerated (`current_projection.py generate` —
  966/966 input digests fresh); its stale `D-R10-MEMORY-1` cutover prose
  re-pointed at `D-R10-MEMORY-2`.
